newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds ease back ahead of election.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds ease back ahead of election.

text.p: Irish bonds eased back slightly in slack trade on Thursday as a variety of worries kept investors sidelined, dealers said.

"It's not surprising that people are cautious, with so many uncertainties about," a dealer said. "On top of worries about EMU and interest rates the Irish market is looking at a close-run general election and pressure on the punt."
By 1500 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down five pence at 101.75 to yield 6.02 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down eight pence at 108.88 to yield 6.67 percent.
Dealers said that yields against German bunds were broadly unchanged from the close at 155 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 89 over in the 10-year.

There was genuine concern about Friday's Irish election resulting in a market-unfriendly hung parliament, dealers said, although latest polls point to a win for the opposition Fianna Fail-Progressive Democrat alliance.
The market on Wednesday shrugged off comments by Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn that there was no immediate need for an interest rate rise.
The market may also have been holding off on Thursday ahead of Irish credit figures due later in the afternoon, dealers said.
European markets were also cautious ahead of U.S. non-farm payroll figures for May due on Friday.

The growth in the U.S. labour force, and allied figures on the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings, could help decide whether the Federal Reserve tightens credit at the next meeting of its monetary policy committee.
Earlier U.S. Treasuries edged higher on news that U.S. jobless claims rose during the last week of May.
